705ef76299e12e809772d522.title_original: Cloud-Edge LLM Collaborative Learning via Accelerating Personalized Bilevel Optimization
705ef76299e12e809772d522.excerpt: arXiv:2609.15664v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Amid the rapid advancement of physical-world intelligence, cloud-edge collaborative large language models (LLMs) have emerged as a promising roadmap for practical LLM deployment. However, existing cloud-edge paradigms struggle to balance global consensus with local personalization, which fails to satisfy the need for a unified knowledge foundation on the cloud and domain-specific adaptation at the edge. To address this, we propose a personalized bilevel optimization framework that formalizes cloud-edge LLM collaboration as a dual structure: the upper level optimizes edge-side personalization, while the lower level governs cloud-side knowledge transfer, reaching cloud-edge evolving in coordination. We then propose CIDERS: while the cloud performs knowledge transfer to the learnable backbone, the key lies in embedding global trajectories into each local personalization step via consensus-variate correction to reconcile personalization with consensus. We provide a comprehensive theoretical analysis, including a geometric characterization of the local trajectory and a full convergence guarantee, revealing an explicit trade-off structure between personalization and global convergence. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-3B and Qwen2-1.5B show CIDERS high performance and can significantly improve the accuracy (as much as 200\%+). Control-state diagnostics further show strong preservation of the local orthogonal component, while

7d44a5a399181468b9699f51.title_original: Hidden not Deleted: How Networks Suppress Entangled Features
7d44a5a399181468b9699f51.excerpt: arXiv:2609.27593v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When a neural network stops reporting a feature, has it forgotten the feature or merely hidden it? Shared representations complicate the answer: removing one feature's direction can also damage another feature. We study this problem in a small autoencoder that compresses and reconstructs inputs, allowing individual feature contributions to be traced directly. With the representation fixed, restoring a single bias partially recovers target detection by exposing a signal hidden behind the output's activation threshold. Tests on target-absent inputs distinguish this recovery from interventions that simply increase output. The same bias intervention becomes less effective when the representation is allowed to change. We find that training only the other outputs can weaken the target's contribution, even without a loss on its own output. A conditional theoretical analysis explains how interference with retained predictions creates this pressure. Yet more flexible predictors still detect residual target information. These findings show how recovery depends on feature geometry and on which parameters are trained, and why a silent output is insufficient evidence of forgetting.

26e4bc135bebd4f776c01307.title_original: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data
26e4bc135bebd4f776c01307.excerpt: arXiv:2609.35348v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Estimating probability densities from a finite set of samples typically requires dataset-specific model fitting. We introduce PRODiGI, a pretrained data-to-program model that infers an explicit, executable generative program in a single forward pass. Pretrained on synthetic datasets paired with their ground-truth programs, PRODiGI accommodates diverse generative families and data dimensionalities through template prediction and non-autoregressive program parameter decoding. Its inferred programs support direct sampling, density and score evaluation, and inspection independently of the pretrained model. We further introduce program-space fine-tuning, which refines differentiable program parameters by maximizing the likelihood of empirical data while keeping model parameters intact. Experiments show that PRODiGI-FT achieves better density and score metrics than existing pretrained models, while offering multi-fold speedups over its closest competitors. Program-space fine-tuning further reduces generation MMD by 90%. By turning empirical data into explicit, reusable programs, PRODiGI introduces a new direction for fast, interpretable tabular generative modeling.

0f2d9c9268d0e1c2a4becdba.title_original: Parameterization method of reservoir properties for ensemble-based data assimilation using intermediate latent space of StyleGAN
0f2d9c9268d0e1c2a4becdba.excerpt: arXiv:2609.39626v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ensemble smoothers are the most successful and efficient techniques currently available for history matching. However, because these methods rely on Gaussian assumptions, their performance is severely degraded when the prior geology is described in terms of complex facies distributions (non-Gaussian). In this way, for these methods, we need to apply efficient parameterization techniques. Currently, the most efficient methods for performing parameterization are deep learning models. However, given the variety of existing deep learning models, studies have not identified which is most suitable for use with ensemble-based methods, although some important models had already been evaluated. Based on a recent literature review, the most promising models selected were VAE-GAN, Latent Diffusion, and StyleGAN models. As a novel aspect of this work, data assimilation with the second generation of StyleGAN (StyleGAN2) model was performed using the latent z-space and intermediate w-space, separately. They were applied in two 2D case studies: one categorical (three facies) and the other continuous. The results demonstrated that all three models are highly efficient, with the StyleGAN2 model standing out for generating samples with geological realism and achieving excellent data matching in the cases studied. Our findings show that performing data assimilation with StyleGAN2 using the intermediate space (w-space) yielded better resu

f0923413af09cd7c1cf5959d.title_original: Cross-Benchmark Transfer from RL on Agentic Coding Tasks
f0923413af09cd7c1cf5959d.excerpt: arXiv:2610.00890v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Coding agents often fail in the last mile: they build most of a feature but drop a requirement, test only the cases their implementation already handles, break behavior that was supposed to stay intact, or validate against an unchecked assumption. We ask whether reinforcement learning (RL) on expert-built agentic coding tasks closes this gap, and whether what the agent learns transfers beyond the training distribution. We post-train Kimi K2.7 Code, a 1T-parameter (32B active) open-weight mixture-of-experts model, with RL alone on 1,700 tasks: 1,000 repository tasks graded by hidden fail-to-pass tests and by pass-to-pass tests of existing behavior, and 700 terminal tasks graded by expert-written hidden verifiers. The reward is the fraction of target checks passed and drops to zero if any pass-to-pass test fails. One epoch of GSPO on a rank-32 LoRA adapter improves pass@1 on each of the six external benchmarks we evaluated, across three agent harnesses: SWE-Bench Pro (60.1 to 64.8), DeepSWE (31.0 to 43.4), Terminal-Bench 2.1 (67.4 to 82.0), Terminal-Bench 3 (1.4 to 12.1), Terminal-Bench 4 (0.0 to 7.6), and SWE-Marathon (5.0 to 25.0). Pooled over the five independent task sets (Terminal-Bench 4 revises Terminal-Bench 3), the improvement is significant (p < 0.001), and it remains significant on the three sets released after the training data was collected (p = 0.004); the model also improves under both harnesses never used

b7663f14f203aa8b8e65999a.title_original: Nearly Optimal Fixed-Confidence Best-Arm Identification with 1-Bit Feedback
b7663f14f203aa8b8e65999a.excerpt: arXiv:2610.02771v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study fixed-confidence best-arm identification under strict 1-bit feedback constraints. At each round, the learner selects an arm and a query set, and receives only a single bit indicating whether the sampled reward belongs to that set. We consider a distribution-free finite-variance setting with arm-wise localization, where direct empirical mean estimation is no longer available and clipping becomes unavoidable. We first formulate a time-uniform 1-bit mean-estimation primitive based on randomized threshold queries and a clipped tail-integral identity. We then embed this primitive into candidate-challenger best-arm identification algorithms. A fixed-clipping algorithm gives a simple anytime $(\epsilon,\delta)$-PAC guarantee, while a phased adaptive-clipping algorithm matches the clipping level to the current resolution and yields a gap-adaptive sample complexity. We also prove a $K$-arm worst-case information-theoretic lower bound showing that the logarithmic penalty caused by finite-variance 1-bit feedback is intrinsic. This bound matches the leading dependence of the phased algorithm up to logarithmic factors.

3e0930525d4046fd9e250680.title_original: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
3e0930525d4046fd9e250680.excerpt: arXiv:2610.03713v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Continual learning treats any drop in performance on previously seen data as forgetting, a convention inherited from settings where the prediction target is stationary. World models violate this assumption: their target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when learned can later become false, and revising it is correct behavior rather than a defect. Non-stationary ground truth is well studied in the concept drift literature and in the temporal factuality of language models, but it has not been formulated for world models, which are distinctive in that they also encode structural knowledge, such as physical laws and object permanence, that must never be degraded. We argue that continual world models need retention stratified by invariance timescale, the time over which knowledge stays true: invariants should be refined but never degraded, while instance-level facts should be revised once the environment changes. We show that standard forgetting metrics, used alone, count correct revision as forgetting and so rank a frozen model highest. We propose differential retention, which reports two quantities separately: invariant retention, checked after every adaptation round, and revision latency, the number of observations a model needs to pick up a change.

f66eeefe3972360ab3650f44.title_original: Inject a Turn, Not a Token: Learning Where to Redirect LLM Reasoning for Self-Correction
f66eeefe3972360ab3650f44.excerpt: arXiv:2610.13672v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models struggle to reliably identify and correct errors in their own reasoning. Unlike prior training-based approaches that fine-tune an LLM to generate revisions or feedback, we learn where to intervene in failed rollouts and determine how to redirect them. To choose where to intervene, we train a 130K-parameter MLP head on a frozen encoder using only final-answer correctness. For redirection, we find that under a fixed generation budget, the tested inline injections fail to reliably redirect reasoning, whereas presenting the same instruction in a new user turn changes the model's course. The resulting correction framework, UPTURN (User-Prompt TURN injection at a learned position), requires no LLM fine-tuning: it retains a selected prefix, injects an instruction as a new user turn, and regenerates the suffix. Across four reasoners and six math benchmarks, UPTURN improves average accuracy in every setting over a 32-rollout baseline. It outperforms self-correction and reflection-token injection baselines under matched correction budgets, transfers across reasoners and to GPQA-Diamond without retraining, and complements GRPO and self-correction methods.

66b719c388f029690ec35de5.title_original: Learning to Read Out: Unembedding Dynamics in Language Model Pretraining
66b719c388f029690ec35de5.excerpt: arXiv:2610.21025v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When does a language model acquire a capability? Developmental studies usually answer this by tracking when models start producing the correct token. But that prediction passes through the unembedding matrix, or readout, which is itself still being learned during pretraining. We show that a model's hidden states can encode task information before its own readout expresses it, so timelines read from outputs conflate what the model encodes with what its readout expresses. To track the readout directly, we introduce parameter-trajectory crosscoding, which fits one sparse dictionary to every token's readout row at every checkpoint. Unlike crosscoders on activations, it needs only checkpoint weights. We use it to locate a narrow early window, 0.4-1.1% of the way through Pythia's pretraining, in which the readout reorganizes and WordNet word categories become decodable from its rows. By then, linear probes on the hidden states already decode task information that the model's own outputs do not yet show. To test whether such gaps depend on how fast the readout learns, we pretrain small models from scratch that differ only in the readout's learning rate. We find that raising it makes the readout develop earlier and the gap close sooner, with little effect on final loss. Together, these results imply that early in training, where many developmental transitions are dated, a behavioral date can reflect when the readout learns to

196a5944d4f0873f595567db.title_original: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
196a5944d4f0873f595567db.excerpt: arXiv:2610.28411v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonstrate improved final accuracy and faster convergence compared to random initialization. Additionally, its frozen embeddings outperform anatomically defined volumetric features on four of five downstream classification tasks and perform competitively with a state-of-the-art foundation model pre-trained on substantially more data. On the independent BrainFMBench benchmark, Brain2Vec ranked first among six pretrained brain MRI foundation models on 9 of 15 sex, age, and BMI prediction tasks across five cohorts. Lastly, we show that Brain2Vec encodes information primarily from a spatially localized and neuroanatomically meaningful set of brain regions, and that manipulating a subset of latent feat

a6d10dcef53ffe964465bc24.title_original: Operationalizing Governed Agentic Workflows in Regulated Finance: A Customer Zero Case Study using Zafin AIOS
a6d10dcef53ffe964465bc24.excerpt: arXiv:2610.33253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Regulated industries such as finance and healthcare face critical governance challenges that hamper the adoption of AI-assisted software development and hinder the transition from experimental pilots to production work. This paper presents Zafin AIOS, an end-to-end orchestration platform and control plane designed to deploy AI within regulated industries such as finance. We provide the architectural principles and an empirical comparison between AI-assisted and human-led workloads. To validate this framework empirically, we conduct a case study analysis of Zafin's internal enterprise workflows, which we refer to as Customer Zero. This paper contributes a production case study of AI-assisted software engineering in regulated industries. We evaluate the results of using Zafin AIOS with two different production codebases, one for the pricing execution platform and the other for the client deal negotiation platform. Our contribution is a customer case study for regulated industries with production codebases and governance, which includes proof of work. The results demonstrate that strictly governed agentic orchestration increases enterprise capacity without compromising control. In the pricing execution platform workflows, the platform provided complete observability and reduced effort by 38\%. In the client deal negotiation platform, it reduced reporting work by 76\% while maintaining all predefined data privacy, role-bas

b2ab7a8dbeef37b6ff8c0d5d.title_original: EmbodiExp: Compositional Experience Transfer for Embodied Agents
b2ab7a8dbeef37b6ff8c0d5d.excerpt: arXiv:2610.39180v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Experience from past tasks can help embodied agents perform new tasks, but it may not remain applicable or effective when conditions change. Tasks with different overall goals often share subgoals, providing a basis for cross-task experience transfer. We present EmbodiExp, a framework for constructing outcome-grounded subgoal experiences and composing them in new tasks. Each experience describes how to pursue a subgoal, when the guidance applies, and what outcome must be verified for completion. Verified outcomes from applying one experience can satisfy the conditions for applying another, allowing experiences from different past tasks to be composed online. By examining the actions and observed outcomes at the subgoal level, EmbodiExp retains experience from successful subgoals and uses explicit action failures to identify actions to avoid under specific conditions. Experiments on EmbodiedBench and VIGIL assess cross-task transfer with experiences kept fixed throughout held-out evaluation. EmbodiExp achieves success rates of 68.0% on EB-Habitat and 68.3% on EB-ALFRED, compared with 50.0% and 54.7% for the agent without stored experience.

d6593ec853806c93e01c250b.title_original: An Axiomatic Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Open Multi-Agent Systems
d6593ec853806c93e01c250b.excerpt: arXiv:2611.03301v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Open multi-agent systems, where only a subset of agents are controllable, are central to real-world domains such as smart grids, yet lack a principled foundation for reinforcement learning algorithm design. We study this setting through n-agent ad hoc teamwork (NAHT), a recent framework for learning in open multi-agent environments. We propose an axiomatic framework that derives value function learning from the Shapley axioms (Efficiency, Symmetry and Linearity), treating them as structural constraints rather than heuristic design choices. This formulation builds on a novel NAHT decomposition, which characterises the fundamental difference between open and fully controllable multi-agent systems, and establishes a cooperative game-theoretic foundation for learning. 7ed792447b736ea2a5b26eb7.excerpt: arXiv:2611.10123v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Can a language model report a pain state it represents? 687f2e810e7c44636c17764e.title_original: Agentic-OPD: Recovering Forgotten Agent Capabilities via On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Tasks
687f2e810e7c44636c17764e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.12799v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning is now the mainstream paradigm for training LLMs on agentic tasks, yet standard practice keeps only the best-validation checkpoint and discards the rest. 8e74fe02bd826ee74f1135f2.title_original: Before Words, Beyond Speech: Evaluating Nonverbal Social Reasoning in Early Childhood
8e74fe02bd826ee74f1135f2.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13213v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Children's earliest years are a period of intense social learning, during which meaning is built through gaze, gesture, and physical contact. To resolve this, \bench introduces a compositional schema that builds atomic interaction cues into progressive levels of social reasoning: contextual, behavioral, interpersonal, and open-ended descriptions. b728a9d379def1e11403fed6.title_original: Deletion Sensitivity Is a Property of the Model: A Three-Condition Measurement over 72 Valid Experimental Cells
b728a9d379def1e11403fed6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13223v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reasoning models write a trace at every turn of a multi-turn tool session, and later turns read it. Upstream providers hold different retention constraints, so a request forwarded across issuers arrives with its history deleted, and its task cost remains unmeasured. This paper reports a direct, blind, multi-seed measurement of full history deletion in multi-turn tool calling, through three rendering conditions, a calibrated set of 72 valid experimental cells, a multi-seed protocol, and the official checker. The same deletion separates the models by direction and by magnitude, one class losing tens of points, another gaining, and a third unchanged, with the endpoint ordering reproduced across seeds and task subsets modulating the magnitude and, near zero, the sign. A re-dosed model preserves its success across the full deletion range, so the reading belongs to the model rather than the dose. Deletion sensitivity is a model-level property under an operational definition, measured under a fixed task family, scorer, and protocol, and a retrained model is a new model that a two-cell screen, one retention run and one deletion run, re-reads for the cost of two runs. Deletion sensitivity is thus a measurable property of the model, and the reading must enter routing as prior information rather than persist as an invisible default cost.

3093b88bb143e960b8905763.title_original: Stochastic Projections and Rank-Aware Learning Rates for Federated LoRA
3093b88bb143e960b8905763.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13331v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Fine-tuning large-scale foundation models across resource-constrained, distributed clients presents significant computational and communication challenges. In this work, we theoretically demonstrate that LoRA fine-tuning with Gaussian initialization and a frozen $\mathbf{A}$ matrix acts as a stochastic approximation of full fine-tuning, where batch gradients are subject to a random, rank-dependent perturbation. Motivated by this insight, we propose freezing and periodically resampling $\mathbf{A}$ matrices at the client level. This strategy decouples the $\mathbf{A}$ and $\mathbf{B}$ gradients, diminishes LoRA low-rank constraints and reduces both computational and uplink communication overheads by 50\%, allowing for the reallocation of resources toward higher adaptation ranks. Furthermore, we show that in this frozen-$\mathbf{A}$ regime, the adaptation rank $r$ directly governs the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) of the perturbed gradients. Specifically, we find that the SNR increases linearly with $r$, implying that clients' learning rates must be dynamically scaled with their adaptation ranks for higher utility. c1d17d65ce09ad3d7651700d.title_original: ForeSpark: Joint Draft and Verification Budget Scheduling for Parallel Speculative Decoding
c1d17d65ce09ad3d7651700d.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13442v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Parallel drafters accelerate LLM decoding by proposing a whole block of draft tokens in a single forward pass, making them attractive for LLM serving. However, these systems control only how many tokens are verified, so every request still drafts a full block. At high serving load, we find that drafting consumes up to 40% of step time, of which a majority is discarded because it is never verified. Yet, draft-length control from autoregressive drafters does not carry over, because a parallel drafter commits to its length before its single pass. Moreover, draft and verification lengths are coupled across the batch, so they must be selected jointly for every request while keeping the decision computationally cheap at every step. In this paper, we propose work-conserving speculation (WCS), a design that jointly allocates draft and verification budgets per request in LLM serving, and present ForeSpark as its prototype. ForeSpark realizes WCS with (i) a context-aware pre-draft estimator that predicts acceptance for every candidate length from the target model's context features, (ii) a lightweight joint draft-verify scheduler that selects both lengths through a global sort, and (iii) a post-draft budget distribution that spends verification on the most promising tokens. da9ef14d67ada93f50013970.title_original: TransGHOST: Real-Time, Synthesis-Free Reconstruction of Instrument-Occluded Regions in Ophthalmic Microsurgery
da9ef14d67ada93f50013970.excerpt: arXiv:2611.13971v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Intraoperative scene perception in ophthalmic microsurgery is limited by instrument occlusion: when a tool enters the high-magnification field, it conceals tissue from both the surgeon and the perception components of robot-assisted systems that process the video. Many video inpainters also depend on future frames and cannot operate online. We present TransGHOST, a causal reference-guided reconstruction pipeline whose non-generative safe mode operates in real time. Every restored value is obtained by resampling a recorded frame using geometric transforms fitted only to visible regions. The system provides per-pixel confidence and provenance and marks unsupported pixels as abstentions. We evaluate TransGHOST on a new veterinary clinical corpus of canine cataract surgery with pixel-level instrument and anatomy labels. Only the occluded region is scored, and each scoring target is verified to differ from the reference supplied to the system. Safe mode reaches 31.89 dB masked PSNR and 0.915 masked SSIM at 51.7 ms median and 85.5 ms 95th-percentile latency. On a pre-declared held-out cohort using instrument cutouts excluded from segmentation training, it reaches 29.83 dB masked PSNR, while matched-mask evaluation on validation shows a 3.45 dB advantage over LaMa. 467292a9d386a40b4bc48be6.title_original: Beyond Attack-Based Accuracy: Rethinking Adversarial Robustness Evaluation Through Structural Gradient Alignment
467292a9d386a40b4bc48be6.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual adversarial robustness remains a fundamental security property as vision systems evolve from conventional classifiers to vision-language models (VLMs) and large vision-language models (LVLMs), with visual inputs remaining an attack surface across generations. Yet existing evaluation methods often depend on prescribed attacks, in-distribution data, extensive probing, or classifier-specific formulations, limiting external auditing of diverse models. We introduce Structural Gradient Alignment (SGA), a complementary robustness metric measuring the structural alignment between input content and objective-conditioned local model sensitivity. SGA uses a few randomly sampled, unlabeled public probes that need not follow the downstream task distribution and only one input-gradient computation per model--probe pair. Across 38 distinct DNNs, VLMs, and LVLMs, SGA produces rankings consistent with attack-based references. Without robustness references, uncalibrated SGA achieves $83.72\%$ average pairwise agreement across eight public-probe conditions, outperforming the strongest overall baseline in all eight by $9.38$ percentage points on average. With known robustness orders of anchor models, calibrated SGA increases agreement to $85.36\%$. 1034b968e11eeb57af422be0.title_original: Evolutionary-based Transfer Learning for Physical Attack on End-to-End Autoencoder Communications
1034b968e11eeb57af422be0.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: End-to-end autoencoder communication has emerged as a promising means of achieving efficient data transmission across various domains. Nevertheless, vulnerabilities have recently been revealed in these systems by adversarial attacks, wherein malevolent entities manipulate the transmitted signals to deceive the autoencoder. This paper leverages the applications of evolutionary algorithms to solve a challenging optimization problem of launching physical attacks against end-to-end autoencoder communication. For white-box scenarios, we introduce PAGA (Physical Attack based on Genetic Algorithm), which combines a genetic algorithm with elite population initialization to craft attack signals that degrade autoencoder performance. To gauge the efficacy of these attack signals, we employ a fitness function that assesses their capacity to induce substantial reconstruction errors and misclassification rates. A Multi-Factorial version of PAGA, referred to as PAMFGA, is proposed to deal with practical scenarios where the attackers have limited knowledge about the receiver, also known as a black-box attack. Our experimental results show that the proposed attacks can substantially degrade the reliability of the considered autoencoder communication systems across the evaluated settings. 01ad8905ba38132f8334c86e.title_original: I2C-GRPO: Insight Importance Checklist for Reinforcement Learning in a Multi-Agent DDoS Alert Triage Workflow
01ad8905ba38132f8334c86e.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17534v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used for investigative tasks over incomplete evidence, such as cybersecurity alert triage, but reinforcement learning (RL) for such tasks is difficult: intermediate steps have no verifiable labels, rollouts are costly, and outcome rewards are sparse. For each decision point, a panel of expert LLMs proposes investigative actions, their atomic forensic insights are extracted, and a separate three-model ranker panel orders the insights by importance. A reward model checks which ranked insights a candidate action targets and returns their consensus-weighted coverage. Because actions are scored without being executed, the reward is a proxy for expected investigative value, and training reduces to a one-step contextual bandit over fixed investigation prefixes. From a soft-computing perspective, the reward is an additive fuzzy measure whose rank-exponent weights act as an ordered weighted averaging (OWA)-type operator; one exponent sets its orness, i.e., how strongly the reward concentrates on the top of the judges' consensus. bbbe33b8f58d60beaaecc80f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study private online allocation problems, where allocation decisions must satisfy differential privacy (DP) to protect sensitive user information while optimizing performance under limited resources. Based on these insights, we propose PPOA, a privacy-preserving meta algorithm for online allocation, and establish sufficient conditions under which PPOA preserves Joint DP (JDP) or Local DP (LDP) while achieving asymptotically near-optimal performance. Building on these conditions, PPOA can be instantiated into a variety of concrete algorithms. In particular, we present the specific designs, which include PPOA-DMD that preserves JDP and LDP and PPOA-FTRL that preserves JDP. We analyze their performance under both adversarial and stochastic settings and characterize the fundamental trade-offs between DP and allocation performance. Finally, we demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed algorithms via numerical experiments on AI model routing in battery-powered edge systems.

c53a71d7707da3b1635dc0f3.title_original: Tractable Importance Sampling for Monte Carlo Privacy Accounting
c53a71d7707da3b1635dc0f3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17596v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluating tight Differential Privacy (DP) parameters for DP matrix factorization with privacy amplification by sampling requires analyzing high-dimensional, correlated Gaussian mixtures. Because integrating these mixture distributions to find the exact privacy failure probability ($\delta$) is analytically intractable, these mechanisms are typically analyzed using Monte Carlo accounting. However, standard sampling suffers from prohibitive variance when estimating small $\delta$ associated with strict privacy guarantees, which in turn requires a large sample complexity, making Monte Carlo accounting inefficient. We demonstrate that Monte Carlo accounting can be made much more efficient via importance sampling. We give a shifted importance sampling proposal distribution parameterized by a stretch factor $\alpha > 1$. We prove a closed-form bound $B(\alpha) < 1$ on the support of the importance-weighted estimator that holds identically for both directions of the hockey-stick divergence, show that $B$ is log-convex so that the optimal $\alpha$ is a one-dimensional root-finding problem, and show that the resulting estimator seamlessly plugs into the KL-Hoeffding verification protocol used by past work, with a sample complexity reduced by exactly a factor of $1/B(\alpha^*)$.

d2f0d9fd8876543290c476a3.title_original: iGRAIL: Blockchain-Based Generative Federated Learning for Trustworthy Healthcare Intelligence
d2f0d9fd8876543290c476a3.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17703v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Healthcare organizations collect huge amounts of patient data from clinical records, medical tests, monitoring systems, and healthcare services. Such data can underpin intelligent healthcare analytics but remains distributed across institutions and cannot be shared directly due to privacy, security, and trust concerns. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative learning without sharing raw patient records, but the exchanged model information remains vulnerable to privacy leakage, tampering, replay, and unauthorized access. In this paper, we propose iGRAIL, a blockchain-enabled generative FL framework for trustworthy healthcare intelligence. iGRAIL combines local generative learning for data augmentation with differential privacy to protect sensitive information during local training. Model communication is secured using cryptographic mechanisms, and blockchain-based verification and smart-contract access control ensure that only authorized, authentic, fresh, and integrity-preserving updates are accepted for federated aggregation. For the two large diabetes datasets, iGRAIL improves accuracy by about 5.4-5.6%, the F1-score by 14.6-16.9%, and MCC by 16.0-18.1% over the best FL or BC-FL baseline.

0bf131f9dea7d3b5a801e706.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Photo-Response Non-Uniformity (PRNU) is the de facto standard trace for sensor-level source-camera attribution, and a high Peak-to-Correlation-Energy (PCE) between a questioned image and a camera reference fingerprint is routinely treated as strong evidence of common origin. 988ca0093903b86072bc07d5.title_original: Inferring Sensitive Events in Multi-Mode Cyber-Physical Systems via Scheduling Side Channels
988ca0093903b86072bc07d5.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many cyber-physical systems (CPS) are multi-mode: they switch between operating modes with different tasksets and timing parameters in response to physical events or user activity. Existing schedule-based attacks and defenses miss this channel because they assume single-mode systems or target a specific, known victim task. We present STAMP, a lightweight attack that needs no knowledge of task parameters or scheduling policy, and works whether or not the system exposes its modes. On a ZoneMinder home-security deployment, STAMP identifies the modes with 94.7% accuracy on unseen hardware, using under 0.5% of one core. On ROS 2 AMCL with the Oxford RobotCar dataset, it identifies which of seven route segments a vehicle traversed with 86.0% accuracy on unseen platforms. A schedule-randomization defense lowers detection recall to 0.53, at which setting only 53.9% as many jobs finish on time. At higher noise ($\epsilon=10$), on-time job completion reduces to 14.4%, while introducing new leakage in 14.1% of the tasksets.

f4deb578112bc1301b202a0a.title_original: LLMs are Vulnerable to Malicious Requests with Indistinguishable Intent
f4deb578112bc1301b202a0a.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Jailbreak attacks can circumvent the safety mechanisms of Large Language Models (LLMs) and lead to the generation of harmful or policy-violating content. We first examine eight jailbreak methods against an LLM-based filter and observe that requests resembling normal user queries tend to have higher filter pass rates than those containing obvious anomalous patterns. This observation motivates the hypothesis that resemblance to normal requests may contribute to jailbreak success. We introduce \textbf{Detail Guidance Attack (DGA)}, a framework that uses an auxiliary LLM to construct detailed requests and interacts with the victim model in a single turn. Across 11 victim models and three datasets, the complete DGA pipeline achieves high attack success rates under our automated judging criterion, including rates above 95\% in several evaluated settings. We also evaluate a DGA-aware filter and conduct a user study on everyday requests with ambiguous or dual-use intent. The survey documents differing expectations about whether models should respond; the usability costs of the filter remain to be measured.

Its design separates workload access, assessment validation, and action authorization so that each boundary produces inspectable records. We evaluate the implementation through a frozen 120-hour non-AI workload and separate desktop and AWS AI cohorts. The workload recorded 999,861 authenticated requests and 999,860 successful responses, with one HTTP 404 and one missing minute representing 139 scheduled requests. 7c77b3495de622771844e5c4.title_original: Game-Theoretic Analysis of RIS-Assisted Challenge-Response PLA - Part II: Partial Channel Knowledge
7c77b3495de622771844e5c4.excerpt: arXiv:2611.17907v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a physical layer authentication scenario in which a legitimate user (Alice) communicates with an authenticator (Bob) through a reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS), controlled by Bob. e46614814899ced37fc262fd.excerpt: arXiv:2611.18312v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Inertial sensors of smartphones are a well-known privacy risk, as they allow inferring sensitive user movements and activity without explicit permissions. Apps deployed on the device can access these signals without user permission, enabling two novel attacks on passenger privacy: First, we are able to determine whether the user is riding an electric train (transport mode detection). Second, we can infer whether other victims are aboard the same train due to shared patterns in the magnetic field (colocation prediction). In an empirical evaluation across 217 train rides, we demonstrate that both attacks are effective, confirming a real-world threat. We discuss countermeasures and argue that magnetometer access should require explicit user permission in mobile operating systems.

f89fd57293ee47c37e98b42f.title_original: Pairing AIS with RF: Analysis of a Markovian Approach for Maritime Data Fusion
f89fd57293ee47c37e98b42f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.18563v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Monitoring maritime activities is important for safety and security, particularly for detecting illegal activities, but remains challenging due to the size and complexity of the maritime domain. The Automatic Identification System (AIS) is commonly used for this purpose, despite its known vulnerabilities. In contrast, space-based radio frequency (RF) observations provide an independent source of vessel activity but lack ship identification and therefore cannot identify vessels on their own. Following the CRISP-DM process, this study applies a Pair Hidden Markov Model (PHMM) to align individual RF detections with AIS trajectories, using temporal and spatial information while modeling noise and timing discrepancies. We evaluate it on NOAA AIS data with synthetic RF detections against nearest-neighbor baselines and analyze its errors with bias tests on trajectory length, sampling density, stationarity and AIS--RF distance. The length-corrected Forward score reaches a top-1 precision of $0.7776$ on the validation split of multi-candidate detections, where errors are possible, and an AUC of $0.637$ for detecting dark vessels among the detections that pass the prefilter. With a single RF detection, the score mostly reflects the AIS trajectory itself, and its errors favor longer and more stationary trajectories. A log-odds score, which compares the full model with a null model without match transitions, raises precision to $0.8580$ a

927bc821849270179eb3f4f1.title_original: Cyber-Zero: Training Cybersecurity Agents without Runtime
927bc821849270179eb3f4f1.excerpt: arXiv:2508.00910v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have achieved remarkable success in software engineering tasks when trained with executable runtime environments, particularly in resolving GitHub issues. However, such runtime environments are often unavailable in other domains, especially cybersecurity, where challenge configurations and execution contexts are ephemeral or restricted. We present Cyber-Zero, the first runtime-free framework for synthesizing high-quality agent trajectories to train cybersecurity LLMs. Cyber-Zero leverages publicly available CTF writeups and employs persona-driven LLM simulation to reverse-engineer runtime behaviors and generate realistic, long-horizon interaction sequences without actual environments. Using trajectories synthesized by Cyber-Zero, we train LLM-based agents that achieve up to 11.4% absolute performance gains over baseline models on three prominent CTF benchmarks: InterCode-CTF, NYU CTF Bench, and Cybench. Our best model, Cyber-Zero-32B, establishes new state-of-the-art performance among open-weight models, matching the capabilities of proprietary systems like DeepSeek-V3-0324 and Claude-3.5-Sonnet while offering superior cost-effectiveness, and demonstrating that runtime-free trajectory synthesis can effectively democratize the development of state-of-the-art cybersecurity agents.

fe0ea901bce129f6fe19e89b.title_original: HackWorld: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Exploiting Web Application Vulnerabilities
fe0ea901bce129f6fe19e89b.excerpt: arXiv:2510.12200v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Web applications are prime targets for cyberattacks as gateways to critical services and sensitive data. Traditional penetration testing is costly and expertise-intensive, making it difficult to scale with the growing web ecosystem. While language model agents show promise in cybersecurity, modern web applications demand visual understanding, dynamic content handling, and multi-step interactions that only computer-use agents (CUAs) can perform. Yet, their ability to discover and exploit vulnerabilities through graphical interfaces remains largely unexplored. We present HackWorld, the first framework for systematically evaluating CUAs' capabilities to exploit web application vulnerabilities via visual interaction. Unlike sanitized benchmarks, HackWorld includes 36 real-world applications across 11 frameworks and 7 languages, featuring realistic flaws such as injection vulnerabilities, authentication bypasses, and unsafe input handling. Using a Capture-the-Flag (CTF) setup, it tests CUAs' capacity to identify and exploit these weaknesses while navigating complex web interfaces. Evaluation of state-of-the-art CUAs reveals concerning trends: exploitation rates below 12% and low cybersecurity awareness. CUAs often fail at multi-step attack planning and misuse security tools. These results expose the current limitations of CUAs in web security contexts and highlight opportunities for developing more security-aware agents capable o

521b5a147e068495b0736b8f.title_original: From TS-SUF-2 to TS-SUF-4: Practical Security Enhancements for FROST2 Threshold Signatures
521b5a147e068495b0736b8f.excerpt: arXiv:2610.02805v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Threshold signature schemes play a vital role in securing digital assets within blockchain and distributed systems. FROST2 stands out as a practical threshold Schnorr signature scheme, noted for its efficiency and compatibility with standard verification processes. However, under the one-more discrete logarithm assumption, with static corruption and centralized key generation settings, FROST2 has been shown by Bellare et al. (in CRYPTO 2022) to achieve only TS-SUF-2 security, which is a consequence of its vulnerability to TS-UF-3 attacks. In this paper, we address this security limitation by presenting an enhanced variant of FROST2, namely, FROST2+ which achieves the TS-SUF-4 security level under the same computational assumptions as the original FROST2. FROST2+ strengthens FROST2 by integrating additional pre-processing token verifications that help mitigate TS-UF-3 and TS-UF-4 vulnerabilities while maintaining practical efficiency. We show that FROST2+ can achieve TS-SUF-4 security not only under the same conditions as the original FROST2 analysis, but also when initialized with a distributed key generation protocol such as PedPoP. Our benchmark using ZCash's FROST library shows that the performance of FROST2+ is comparable to FROST2 and about 64-79% faster than FROST when precomputation is enabled.

753f0036f84cbaa1893cd054.title_original: They Will See Johnny's Message: A Measurement Study of Post-Quantum Cryptography Across Email Delivery Paths
753f0036f84cbaa1893cd054.excerpt: arXiv:2610.36145v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Harvest-now, decrypt-later (HNDL) attacks make the transition to post-quantum cryptography (PQC) urgent for email. This paper presents a systematic measurement that jointly examines PQC deployment across email service stages, negotiation by communicating peers, and usable message encryption. Endpoint-level support alone does not establish PQC readiness across email workflows because submission, relay, and access use independently negotiated Transport Layer Security (TLS) connections. We therefore combine three snapshots of relay, submission, access, and webmail services associated with the Tranco Top~1M domains with controlled tests of mail clients, sending servers, and OpenPGP and S/MIME implementations. Our measurements reveal a transition concentrated among a few providers, with available capability not consistently translating into actual use. Fewer than half of the domains in each service panel support PQC, and Google alone accounts for approximately 87\% of hybrid-capable relay domains. Only two of eight tested sending providers negotiate PQC with our receiver, although five accept it inbound. When TLS groups are restricted to PQC, four of the six incompatible senders fall back to plaintext where unencrypted SMTP remains permitted. At the message layer, limited native key generation, key-format incompatibilities, and backend integration failures further constrain usable PQC encryption.

70d1d81bc2382ad99f741b8f.title_original: VerfGraph: Efficient Zero-Knowledge Verifiable Graph Query Evaluation System
70d1d81bc2382ad99f741b8f.excerpt: arXiv:2611.04240v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graph databases are widely used to manage relationship-rich data and support multi-hop traversal and shortest-path queries in applications such as financial risk control and social networks. When a client issues such queries to a database owner, the returned result may be incorrect. However, the client cannot directly verify it because the graph is typically large and private, making re-executing the query both infeasible and insecure. Verifiable and confidential graph query evaluation thus plays an important role in such applications. We present VerfGraph, a zero-knowledge verifiable graph query evaluation system, which enables a client to verify that the query result was correctly computed over a committed graph, without revealing anything beyond the public inputs and what is implied by the query result. While adopting the expansion-centric operator model introduced by ZKGraph (ICDE'26), VerfGraph improves both proving efficiency and query expressiveness in two key ways. First, we propose new proof methods for the core operators in ZKGraph, such as graph expansion and shortest path, that require substantially fewer expensive comparisons and eliminate edge canonicalization for bidirectional edge relations. Second, we introduce dedicated proofs for count and weighted shortest-path operators, which ZKGraph does not support, broadening the class of graph queries that can be verified. We evaluate VerfGraph using the LDBC Social

c2f1a109e1fa8fd43a6299bf.title_original: Training Language Model Agents to Find Vulnerabilities with CTF-Dojo
c2f1a109e1fa8fd43a6299bf.excerpt: arXiv:2508.18370v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated exceptional capabilities when trained within executable runtime environments, notably excelling at software engineering tasks through verified feedback loops. Yet, scalable and generalizable execution-grounded environments remain scarce, limiting progress in training more capable ML agents. We introduce CTF-Dojo, the first large-scale executable runtime tailored for training LLMs with verifiable feedback, featuring 658 fully functional Capture-The-Flag (CTF)-style challenges containerized in Docker with guaranteed reproducibility. To enable rapid scaling without manual intervention, we develop CTF-Forge, an automated pipeline that transforms publicly available artifacts into ready-to-use execution environments in minutes, eliminating weeks of expert configuration traditionally required. We trained LLM-based agents on just 486 high-quality, execution-verified trajectories from CTF-Dojo, achieving up to 9.9% absolute gains over strong baselines across three competitive benchmarks: InterCode-CTF, NYU CTF Bench, and Cybench. Our best-performing 32B model reaches 31.9% Pass@1, establishing a new open-weight state-of-the-art that rivals frontier models like DeepSeek-V3-0324 and Gemini-2.5-Flash. a123afde9b09aeb4b3c00aa6.title_original: Adversarial Attacks on Downstream Weather Forecasting Models: Application to Tropical Cyclone Trajectory Prediction
a123afde9b09aeb4b3c00aa6.excerpt: arXiv:2510.10140v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Deep learning-based weather forecasting (DLWF) models leverage past weather observations to generate future forecasts, supporting a wide range of downstream applications, including tropical cyclone (TC) prediction. In this paper, we investigate the vulnerability of these models to adversarial attacks, where subtle perturbations to upstream forecasts can alter downstream TC trajectory predictions. Crafting perturbed inputs to steer downstream outputs toward attacker-specified trajectories is a challenging problem for several reasons. First, conventional TC detection systems are opaque, non-differentiable black boxes, making standard gradient-based attacks infeasible. Second, the extreme rarity of TC events leads to a severe class imbalance problem, making it difficult to develop attack methods that produce realistic-looking cyclone paths aligned with target trajectories. To overcome these limitations, we propose Cyc-Attack, a novel method for perturbing the forecasts of DLWF models to generate adversarial trajectories. The proposed method uses a differentiable surrogate model to approximate the TC detector's output, enabling the application of gradient-based attacks. Cyc-Attack also employs a skewness-aware loss function with a kernel dilation strategy to address the severe class imbalance problem. Distance-based gradient weighting and regularization strategies are also introduced to constrain perturbations to eliminate

371e6942f927f423c6579f5d.title_original: Denoising the US Census: Succinct Block Hierarchical Regression
371e6942f927f423c6579f5d.excerpt: arXiv:2603.10099v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The 2020 United States Census adopted differential privacy to protect individual confidentiality, adding calibrated noise to summary demographic measurements that are then reconciled into population tables. We developed BlueDown, a postprocessing algorithm that combines techniques from linear regression and constrained optimization while exploiting measurement structure for efficiency. On 2020 Census data, BlueDown reduced the error of groupings by race at the county level by 21-36% and of all county-level groupings by 9-58%; at the tract level, it reduced error of groupings by housing type by 38-61%. These gains came at no cost to confidentiality or computational efficiency, and would improve the validity of research relying on this definitive dataset and analyses used to guide the distribution of over $1.5 trillion in annual federal spending.

aaba9e6b332c2478eefd28de.title_original: ECGGuard: Deep Watermarking of Electrocardiogram Signals With Error-Correcting
aaba9e6b332c2478eefd28de.excerpt: arXiv:2610.13357v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Wearable electrocardiogram (ECG) recordings pass through multiple networks and systems before automated interpretation, leaving patient metadata vulnerable to loss. Digital watermarking can embed this metadata in the signal, but conventional methods fail under time shifts, and high waveform similarity does not guarantee the same downstream diagnosis. A fully convolutional generator embeds the payload without signal quantization, a detector decodes the message frame by frame and checks for watermark presence, and during training a frozen arrhythmia classifier penalizes changes that would alter its predictions. 07822f31859abc92c2308112.title_original: SoK: Assessing Post-Quantum Cryptography Adoption in Software Development: Standards, Lifecycle Coverage, Deployment Maturity, and Evidence of Readiness
07822f31859abc92c2308112.excerpt: arXiv:2611.08442v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Standardised post-quantum cryptography (PQC) is critical for protecting software systems against future quantum threats, but standardised algorithms alone do not provide a pathway for their secure integration into software. This paper presents a Systematisation of Knowledge (SoK) of PQC integration in software development, synthesising existing approaches across implementation, migration, and developer education. We analyse these approaches against NIST PQC standards and PQC migration guidance, software development lifecycle coverage, cybersecurity practices, deployment maturity, and testing and evaluation evidence. Our analysis shows that existing work establishes important technical and organisational foundations but provides disconnected support across the software development lifecycle, with limited coordination between preparation, implementation, migration, deployment, maintenance, and developer practices. Evaluation evidence also remains concentrated in controlled or early-stage settings, providing stronger evidence of technical feasibility than operational readiness. We identify cross-cutting gaps and research directions for developing lifecycle-oriented, empirically validated approaches that connect technical, developer, and organisational requirements for secure PQC integration.

64e887f7747f822f330d6e06.background_ko: Google은 연말 선물 구매와 여행 계획, 각종 준비로 바쁜 이용자의 일정 관리를 돕기 위해 Ask Maps 기능을 확대한다고 설명했다.

0d094b599efebfdaa0f738e7.title_original: Hugging Face and OpenRouter join forces to make open-weight models easy to run
0d094b599efebfdaa0f738e7.title_ko: Hugging Face, 언어모델 추론 라우터를 OpenRouter로 전환
0d094b599efebfdaa0f738e7.summary_ko: Hugging Face가 언어모델 추론 요청을 OpenRouter로 보내 가격·속도·안정성에 따라 제공업체를 선택하고, 실패하면 다른 업체로 재시도하도록 전환했다. 기존 코드와 Hugging Face 토큰은 유지되지만, 언어모델 요청에는 사용자가 등록한 제공업체 API 키를 더 이상 쓸 수 없다. 이미지·영상·오디오 생성은 기존 방식대로 처리된다.
0d094b599efebfdaa0f738e7.background_ko: 기존 Inference Providers는 선택한 제공업체에서 요청이 실패하면 다른 업체로 재시도하지 않고 오류를 반환했다.

curation.reason_ko: Hugging Face와 OpenRouter가 오픈웨이트 모델 실행을 쉽게 하는 협력을 발표했다.

059ec74baba0bfdb603e1be7.excerpt: Hackers who breached the cloud environment of network and email security company Barracuda earlier this month used a stolen cloud access key and the ARTEX AI penetration testing framework. [...]
059ec74baba0bfdb603e1be7.title_ko: Barracuda, 클라우드 침해에 ARTEX AI 침투 테스트 도구 사용됐다고 밝혀
059ec74baba0bfdb603e1be7.summary_ko: Barracuda는 11월 1~2일 44시간 동안 클라우드 계정 약 10개가 침해됐으며, 공격에 ARTEX AI 침투 테스트 프레임워크가 쓰였다고 밝혔다. 고객 연동 자격증명 보관 시스템에도 공격자가 접근했지만 해당 정보의 열람·탈취 증거는 찾지 못했다. 회사는 잠재적 영향 고객에게 직접 통보하고 연동 자격증명의 폐기·재발급을 요청했다.
059ec74baba0bfdb603e1be7.background_ko: Barracuda는 프로젝트 종료 후 폐기하지 않은 협력사용 클라우드 접근 키가 협력사 GitHub 저장소의 설정 파일에 보관돼 있었으며, 이 키가 탈취된 것으로 추정했다.

curation.reason_ko: Barracuda 클라우드 침해에 탈취한 접근 키와 ARTEX가 사용됐다는 보도가 나왔다.

bb3a645f0406ad67dfd31df0.title_original: Microsoft says months-old bug caused global Microsoft 365 outage
bb3a645f0406ad67dfd31df0.excerpt: Microsoft says a software bug introduced in July caused last week's worldwide Microsoft 365 outage, triggering a cascading failure that left more than 80% of its networking gateway servers unresponsive. [...]
bb3a645f0406ad67dfd31df0.title_ko: Microsoft, 전 세계 Microsoft 365 장애 원인으로 7월 도입된 버그 지목
bb3a645f0406ad67dfd31df0.summary_ko: Microsoft는 11월 12~13일 약 24시간 이어진 Microsoft 365 장애로 Outlook·Teams·Copilot 등이 영향을 받았다고 밝혔다. 예비 조사에 따르면 서버 간 트래픽 재분배가 연쇄 장애로 이어져 한때 네트워크 게이트웨이 서버의 80% 이상이 응답하지 않았다. 회사는 수정사항을 배포해 복구했으며 용량 증설과 모니터링·안전장치 강화 조치를 취했다고 설명했다.
bb3a645f0406ad67dfd31df0.background_ko: Microsoft의 예비 조사에 따르면 7월 업데이트에 포함된 잠복 버그가 Teams의 인프라 전환에 따른 트래픽 증가와 서버 용량 감소가 겹치면서 촉발됐다.

curation.reason_ko: Microsoft가 세계적 365 장애를 수개월 전 도입된 버그와 게이트웨이 연쇄 장애로 설명했다.

e97521ee298f92ad2778ef69.title_ko: Fandango 결제 페이지에 카드 스키머…카드번호·CVV 등 노출
e97521ee298f92ad2778ef69.summary_ko: Fandango는 2026년 10월 8~11일 공식 웹사이트에서 결제한 일부 고객의 카드번호, CVV, 유효기간, 청구지 우편번호와 이메일이 노출됐을 수 있다고 통지했다. 회사는 결제 페이지 문제를 수정했으며, 피해 고객 수는 공개하지 않았고 유출 정보가 악용된 사기 사례도 아직 파악하지 못했다고 밝혔다.
e97521ee298f92ad2778ef69.background_ko: 결제 페이지에 삽입된 카드 스키밍 코드가 주문 과정에서 입력된 결제 정보를 가로채 공격자에게 전송했다.

curation.reason_ko: Fandango가 결제 페이지에 입력된 카드정보 노출 사고를 고객에게 통지하고 있다.

ee374813c11c1d0dbbebcca5.excerpt: The FBI's latest CJIS Security Policy requires law enforcement agencies to strengthen password protections and enforce MFA across privileged and non-privileged accounts. Specops Software outlines seven practical steps to meet these requirements, block compromised passwords, and maintain compliance. [...]
ee374813c11c1d0dbbebcca5.title_ko: 법집행기관을 위한 CJIS 비밀번호·다중요소인증 준수 지침
ee374813c11c1d0dbbebcca5.summary_ko: FBI의 CJIS 보안정책에 맞춰 법집행기관이 비밀번호와 다중요소인증(MFA)을 관리하는 7가지 방법을 소개한다. 취약·유출 비밀번호 차단과 정기 점검, 전송·저장 시 보호, 일반·관리자 계정과 각종 접속 방식에 대한 MFA 적용을 다루며, 서로 다른 두 인증 요소를 사용하는 AAL2 요건도 설명한다.
ee374813c11c1d0dbbebcca5.background_ko: 비밀번호 탈취와 MFA 적용 공백이 주요 침입 경로로 남아 있는 가운데, FBI의 CJIS 보안정책은 관련 통제를 즉시 이행해야 하는 우선순위 요건으로 규정하고 있다.

8d83349efd499e32eb886cb2.excerpt: Threat actors are now relying on agentic workflows powered by AI-based offensive frameworks to automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation, accelerating attacks to machine speed. [...]
8d83349efd499e32eb886cb2.title_ko: Google, AI 에이전트 공격 자동화 확인…완전 자율 공격 확대 전망
8d83349efd499e32eb886cb2.summary_ko: Google 위협정보그룹(GTIG)은 공격자들이 AI 에이전트로 취약점 탐지와 악용을 사람의 개입 없이 자동화한 사례를 확인했다고 밝혔다. 연구진은 보고 시점부터 3개월 내 개입이 거의 필요 없는 단순 공격, 6개월 내 정교한 완전 자율 공격이 등장할 가능성이 있다고 전망했다. 공격 자동화가 방어자의 패치 대응 시간을 줄이고 있다는 경고도 내놨다.
8d83349efd499e32eb886cb2.background_ko: GTIG에 따르면 금전 목적 및 국가 지원 공격집단이 AI 기반 공격 프레임워크를 대규모로 도입하면서 취약점 탐지와 악용을 자동화하고 있다.

curation.reason_ko: Google이 AI 에이전트 기반 취약점 탐색·악용 자동화와 공격 가속을 경고했다.

3146c48ebd18323885f4ceac.excerpt: Coles Group Limited, Australia's second-largest retailer, is investigating what it described as a "cyber security incident" that has not impacted the company's stores. [...]
3146c48ebd18323885f4ceac.title_ko: 호주 유통업체 Coles, 사이버 사고 조사…현재까지 정보 유출 증거 없어
3146c48ebd18323885f4ceac.summary_ko: 호주 유통업체 Coles가 사이버보안 사고를 조사하며 외부 전문가 및 호주 사이버보안센터와 대응하고 있다. 회사는 현재까지 고객·직원·공급업체 정보가 침해되거나 유출된 증거를 발견하지 못했으며, 매장과 온라인 쇼핑·멤버십 서비스는 정상 운영 중이라고 밝혔다. 사고 발견 시점과 공격자의 금전 요구 여부는 공개되지 않았다.

e8ca9a741af35f0bb5ad38e2.excerpt: Anthropic recently rolled out Claude Mythos 5.2 to selected partners and Fable 5.2 to regular users, with improvements to coding and reasoning. But we also noticed some interesting cybersecurity changes. [...]
e8ca9a741af35f0bb5ad38e2.title_ko: Anthropic, Fable 5.2 보안 요청 오차단 감소·Mythos 취약점 탐지 향상 발표
e8ca9a741af35f0bb5ad38e2.summary_ko: Anthropic은 일반 사용자용 Claude Fable 5.2에서 보안 관련 요청의 불필요한 차단이 이전 버전보다 약 60% 줄었다고 밝혔다. 파트너용 Mythos 5.2는 취약점 탐지·재현·수정 능력이 Fable 5.2보다 우수하다고 설명했다. 다만 Fable의 고위험 보안 작업 제한은 유지되며, 회사는 출시 전 평가로 모든 실패 가능성을 포착할 수 없다고 인정했다.
e8ca9a741af35f0bb5ad38e2.background_ko: Anthropic은 같은 기반 모델을 사용하더라도 일반 사용자용 Fable과 고급 보안 업무용 Mythos의 용도가 달라 안전장치를 차등 적용했다.

curation.reason_ko: Claude 새 모델의 보안 작업 거부와 취약점 탐색 능력 변화가 보도돼 활용·통제 양쪽에 의미가 있다.

724380ea11e6f3810f08bf90.title_original: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
724380ea11e6f3810f08bf90.excerpt: An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability, dubbed NoisyTCP, affects almost all Linux distributions and lets attackers crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations. [...]
724380ea11e6f3810f08bf90.title_ko: Linux 커널 취약점 NoisyTCP, 인증 없이 원격 서버 충돌 유발
724380ea11e6f3810f08bf90.summary_ko: 보안 연구자 Hyunwoo Kim이 Linux 커널의 원격 서비스 거부 취약점 NoisyTCP(CVE-2026-99288)를 공개했다. 조작된 TCP 패킷으로 인증 없이 커널 충돌을 유발할 수 있지만 데이터 변조나 임의 코드 실행으로 이어지지는 않으며, 수정 패치가 제공됐다.
724380ea11e6f3810f08bf90.background_ko: 잠금 없는 소켓 조회 과정의 경쟁 상태로 재사용된 소켓 메모리에 초기화 전에 접근하면서 NULL 포인터 역참조가 발생하는 것이 원인이다.

curation.reason_ko: 여러 Linux 배포판의 기본 서버 구성을 중단시킬 수 있다는 NoisyTCP 취약점이 보도됐다.

f87fb7aeb1b1ebf020609828.excerpt: The attacker stole an access key from Fireworks and used it to exfiltrate credentials that enabled them to push malicious Claude Code extension copies. The post Cursor Supply Chain Attack Started at Fireworks AI appeared first on SecurityWeek .

f87fb7aeb1b1ebf020609828.background_ko: Cursor에 따르면 공격자는 Fireworks AI에서 유출된 접근 키로 읽기 전용 저장소에 접근하고, 그 안의 가려지지 않은 자격증명을 이용해 침투 범위를 넓혔다.

curation.reason_ko: Fireworks의 접근 키 탈취가 악성 Claude Code 확장 배포로 이어진 공급망 경로가 보도됐다.

6cebb09b0a2a9ddd2f4efb96.title_original: Rapid7 Detected Exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center, N-able N-central also Exploited
6cebb09b0a2a9ddd2f4efb96.excerpt: Overview On November 6, 2026, the Apache Software Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-90436 , a critical unsafe reflection vulnerability ( CWE-470 ) in Axis 1.x that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE). Apache Axis is a Simple Object Access Protocol (SOAP) implementation used for the creation of Java Web services. CISA has assigned CVE-2026-90436 a CVSS score of 9.8 Critical . Since the initial November 6 disclosure, it has transpired that some versions of Atlassian Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central use the affected Axis library and are vulnerable to CVE-2026-90436. Both products require a non-default configuration in order to be vulnerable. CVE-2026-90436 is now being actively exploited in the wild against both known affected products. On November 13, 2026, Rapid7 MDR detected exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center in a customer environment. Separately, on November 13, 2026, N-able reported exploitation in the wild against N-central for a vulnerability that strongly correlates to CVE-2026-90436. A proof-of-concept exploit that leverages CVE-2026-90436 and targets N-central was published on November 12, 2026, as part of a series of public zero-day disclosures against N-central. Rapid7 recommends remediating exposed systems on an emergency basis outside of normal patching cycles. 6cebb09b0a2a9ddd2f4efb96.summary_ko: Rapid7은 Apache Axis의 비인증 원격 코드 실행 취약점 CVE-2026-90436을 악용한 Confluence Data Center 공격을 탐지했다고 밝혔다. N-able도 N-central에서 해당 취약점과 연관성이 높은 공격을 보고했으며, 두 제품 모두 특정 비기본 설정에서 영향을 받는다. Confluence는 9.2.28 등으로 업데이트하고, N-central은 Legacy API 비활성화 등 공급사 지침을 따라야 한다.

An attacker with view-only access to a document can chain vulnerabilities in ONLYOFFICE Docs to execute arbitrary operating system commands as root inside the official DocumentServer container. The findings also expose server files and document data that the viewer never displays, even when downloading is disabled. The changelog describes the release's security changes. Proof-of-concept code is available on the accompanying Github repository . It supports collaborative editing and can integrate with applications that store and share files. 7f022dc18f76e8f2488a1b77.title_ko: ONLYOFFICE Docs 취약점 5건…열람 권한만으로 컨테이너 root 권한 획득 가능

96255e53b21a719c0af6fa9b.title_original: VU#604762: Multiple vendors vulnerable to Unicode Normalization Collision on macOS (APFS)
96255e53b21a719c0af6fa9b.excerpt: Overview A mismatch between Apple File System (APFS) filesystem and path resolution for multiple applications allows attackers to bypass security exclusions using alternative Unicode spellings. By supplying an alternative Unicode spelling or case-folded variant (such as ß versus ss ) that bypasses the application's file write checks, a local attacker can overwrite files wherever the process has write permissions, potentially leading to data corruption, configuration hijacking, or code execution. Multiple vendors have assigned CVEs and issued patches to address this flaw. Description Several archive tools, packaging systems, and runtimes enforce exclusion filters using pathname comparisons that do not match the underlying filesystem's resolution behavior. By using a byte-for-byte comparison (such as ß versus ss ), rather than full case folding, a vulnerable application can be tricked into silently overwriting protected files. This vulnerability exposes backup tools, forensic workflows, and CI/CD pipelines to unauthorized file modification. The CVEs assigned during coordination are as follows: CVE-2026-14978 HashiCorp go-slug could allow an attacker with local filesystem access to bypass .terraformignore exclusions and cause sensitive files to be included in Terraform slug uploads due to improper handling of Unicode normalization during path matching. 96255e53b21a719c0af6fa9b.summary_ko: CERT/CC는 APFS의 파일명 해석과 애플리케이션의 경로 비교 방식이 달라 파일 제외 규칙과 접근 제한을 우회할 수 있다고 경고했다. Deno·Libarchive·setuptools·HashiCorp go-slug 등이 관련되며, 파일 덮어쓰기나 배포물에 민감 파일이 포함되는 문제가 발생할 수 있어 영향받는 소프트웨어의 업데이트를 권고했다.

fdb63537b71bcfb54ebfa3d8.summary_ko: ffmpeg-skill은 Claude Code, Cursor, Codex에서 사용할 수 있는 로컬 영상 편집 저장소로, FFmpeg 도구 42개와 기계 판독형 규약, MCP 서버를 제공한다. 영상 자르기, 자막, 화면 재구성, 음량 조정과 플랫폼별 내보내기를 지원하며 클라우드나 API 키가 필요 없다고 소개한다.

curation.reason_ko: 코딩 에이전트가 로컬 FFmpeg 도구 42개를 쓰도록 지원하며, 당일 별 475개가 확인됐다.

5eedc2334a2fdc0c5c8aa4d2.excerpt: PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.
5eedc2334a2fdc0c5c8aa4d2.title_ko: PaperOrchestra, 다중 에이전트 기반 AI 연구 논문 작성 자동화 프레임워크
5eedc2334a2fdc0c5c8aa4d2.summary_ko: PaperOrchestra는 AI 연구 논문 작성을 자동화하는 프레임워크다. 여러 에이전트를 활용하는 구조로, 저장소 이름은 google-research/paper-orchestra다.

curation.reason_ko: AI 연구 논문 작성을 자동화하는 다중 에이전트 프레임워크로, 당일 별 306개가 확인됐다.
